about: THE SYNTAX TABLE: what the page's editor (CodeMirror 6) and the Mac app's editor (TextKit 2) colour, written once.
A syntax is a list of RULES; a rule is a regular expression and a ROLE (a name for what the text is: a heading, a link, a key...).
A client turns a role into a colour: the page through the CSS custom properties it makes from `roles` below, the Mac app through its theme
(`category` is the CotEditor theme category the role takes its colour from; `light` and `dark` are the colours when no theme is found).
ENGINE, the same in every client (tests/test_syntax_table.py runs cases.json through a Python copy, the page and the app run the same file):
1. A markdown document may start with a front matter: a first line `frontMatter.open`, then lines up to one of `frontMatter.close`; it is coloured by the syntax named in `frontMatter.syntax`.

2. Lines that open or close a fenced block (up to three spaces, then one of `fences.markers`, three characters) toggle code: the text between two fence lines, and the fence lines, take the role `fences.role` (a closing fence is ANY fence line: parity).
3. Everything else gets the rules of the syntax, in order; where two rules colour the same characters the LATER rule wins. A rule matches inside one line.
THE REGULAR EXPRESSIONS are read by three engines (ICU, JavaScript, Python), so they use a common subset, and tests/test_syntax_table.py rejects the rest:
explicit classes only (no \w \d \s \b, no \p{..}: they differ between the engines for non-ASCII text); `^` and `$` mean the start and end of a LINE;

no flags (the engines set the multiline one), no named groups, lookbehind only with a fixed width; no rule may match a line break; offsets in cases.json are UTF-16 units (the page's and the Mac's own).
`frontMatter.scan` is how many characters from the top are searched for the closing line (a front matter is short; a stray --- at the top of a long file is not one).

roles.help: keys of a YAML front matter
